title: BR/EIDGING OPERA
program_note:
BR/EIDGING OPERA is intended as a “bridge” between Western Classical music and that of “Beijing” opera.  It was written for a dance-drama created by Mr. Zhou Jing-Qiu of the Beijing City Opera Company, and is dedicated to him.

The dance-drama, on one level, is about the individual in society.  In the music, the individual is characterized by ordinary muted string instruments, while the society is characterized by the same instruments which have been prepared to distort the sound.  The core ensemble of BR/EIDGING OPERA should be thought of as three groups of three, each made up of an ordinary string instrument, a prepared instrument, and a double-reed instrument.  (The only difference between the groups is the range:  Violins with Oboe, Violas with English Horn, and Violoncellos with Bassoon; the arrangement of the instruments on the stage should reflect that organization, as shown below).  This grouping of instruments is meant to portray the fact that the individual and society are inseparable, different sides of the same being.

David S. Lefkowitz

October 13, 1998Los Angeles, CA
